messages.subject: 2-colour heatmap
parts:
Hi All,

First off, thanks to Hadley for a terrific package. For routine plots
and for many not-so-routine, the learning curve is quite gentle. I
nonetheless have run into difficulty generating the heatmap described
below.

I would like to generate a 2-colour heatmap plot with values > 0 in
one gradient colour and values <= 0 in another color.

This code generates the plot for the positive values and leaves the
negative ones blank:

ggplot(my.data[my.data$Signal > 0, ], aes(my.group, my.row)) +
geom_tile(aes(fill = Signal),
colour = "white") + scale_fill_gradient(low = "white", high =
"steelblue")

This code generates the plot for the negative values and leaves the
positive ones blank:

# I reverse the gradient here because it is the absolute values that
are of interest
# i.e., a large absolute value corresponds to a high signal
ggplot(my.data[my.data$Signal <= 0, ], aes(my.group, my.row)) +
geom_tile(aes(fill = (Signal)),
colour = "white") + scale_fill_gradient(low = "yellow", high =
"white")

What I would like is a “merging” of the 2 plots. I realize that this
cannot be done literally and so I’ve experimented with subsetting and
the like using layering but have been unable to achieve what I want.
I’m guessing that this must be straight-forward but I haven’t
sufficiently wrapped my head around the grammar structure just yet to
get it right.

I also want to be able to do the following:

1. Order the x and y axis values in a specified order rather than in
the default alphabetical listing.
2. Set the gradient intervals for the 2 colours to be the same.

Many thanks. -Bob

Here are a few lines of the data:

> What I would like is a ï¿½mergingï¿½ of the 2 plots. I realize that this

> Iï¿½m guessing that this must be straight-forward but I havenï¿½t

> sufficiently wrapped my head around the grammar structure just yet to

What about scale_gradient2?

(untested):

ggplot(my.data, aes(my.group, my.row)) +
geom_tile(aes(fill = Signal), colour = "white") +
scale_fill_gradient2(low = "yellow", mid="white", high = "steelblue")

> I also want to be able to do the following:
>
> 1. Order the x and y axis values in a specified order rather than in
> the default alphabetical listing.

Make my.group and my.row be factors, with levels in the order you want
them to appear.
> 2. Set the gradient intervals for the 2 colours to be the same.

Probably setting the limits argument to scale_fill_gradient2 to be
symmetric would work. Something like
limits=c(-1,1)*max(abs(my.data$Signal)) might work.

>
> Many thanks. -Bob
>
> Here are a few lines of the data:

FYI, a few rows are not nearly as helpful as a (sufficient subset) of
the data in dput format (or some format which will create an actual
object to use). With that, I probably would have tested my solutions :)

--
Brian S. Diggs, PhD
Senior Research Associate, Department of Surgery
Oregon Health & Science University
